question: {Simplify: } (sqrt{75} - sqrt{108} + sqrt{6075})²
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factor out perfect squares to express all terms as multiples of √3.

√75 = 5√3, √108 = 6√3, √6075 = 45√3

Expression = (5√3 − 6√3 + 45√3)²

Sum inside bracket = 44√3

Square the sum = (44√3)² = 1936 × 3 = 5808

**∴ The correct answer is 5808.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(√75 − √108 + √6075)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simplifying each surd independently:

⇒ √75 = √(25 × 3) = 5√3

⇒ √108 = √(36 × 3) = 6√3

⇒ √6075 = √(2025 × 3) = 45√3

⇒ Substituting the simplified surds back into the expression:

⇒ (5√3 − 6√3 + 45√3)²

⇒ Grouping the terms together:

⇒ [(5 − 6 + 45)√3]²

⇒ [44√3]²

⇒ Squaring both parts inside the bracket:

⇒ 44² × (√3)²

⇒ 1936 × 3 = 5808

**∴ The correct answer is 5808.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Surds

The multiplication property √(a × b) = √a × √b helps extract perfect squares to simplify complex roots easily.

Perfect Squares

Memorising squares of numbers up to 50 is extremely useful. For example, knowing 45² = 2025 instantly identifies √6075 as 45√3.

BODMAS / PEMDAS Rule

Always simplify the operations inside the Brackets first before applying the exponent (power of 2) to the overall expression.
